title: Hideo Kojima Says He’s Aware Of His Mortality As He Celebrates 63rd Birthday
description: Game designer Hideo Kojima celebrates his 63rd birthday today, August 24, and he does not plan to pack it up anytime soon. Posting on social media, Kojima said he is aware he will not live forever--in fact he already knows how he wants to die--so he is being particularly thoughtful about how he spends his time. "As I get older, the things I 'have to do' and the things I 'want to do' continue to increase. At the same time, the time I 'have to do them' continues to decrease," he said. "I constantly need to reassess how I use my time and how I live my life. That said, once you’ve taken something on, you can’t simply put it down and walk away." Kojima also pointed out that 2026 marks his 40th anniversary of making games, having begun his professional career in 1986. Additionally, 2026 represents the 10th anniversary of Kojima Productions, the studio he founded after leaving Konami. At the latter, he ran an internal unit also called Kojima Productions. Also in his post, Kojima said he wants to "remain focused on creating games," even though he is receiving "various opportunities and offers" to do other things. He didn't elaborate as to what these might be, but it was previously reported that Kojima was asked if he wanted to direct the Death Stranding movie before he opted to sit out and let Michael Sarnoski direct. Kojima has a number of projects currently in the works, including the espionage game Physint and the horror game OD. Kojima Productions seemingly updated Death Stranding 2's night sky scene to honor Kojima's birthday. https://twitter.com/KojiPro2015_EN/status/2091542178581598674 What's more, Kojima's staff got him a pretty boss cake--check it out below, along with a photo of Kojima and his friend Geoff Keighley. https://twitter.com/KojiPro2015_EN/status/2091800610727485665 https://twitter.com/geoffkeighley/status/2091548542426837361

title: Mortal Shell 2 Players Really Hate Those Bear Traps, And So Do I
description: Mortal Shell 2 has a lot of tough enemies waiting to knock you out of your shell and stuff your carcass into a coffin. Many of them are terrifying because of their difficulty, ugliness, or both. Still, nothing compares to the greatest enemy developer Cold Symmetry made for the souls-like action-RPG: those gosh-dang bear traps. Danger lurks around every corner in this game. Walk here, and you might get ambushed by a rabid miner just itching to stab you with a pickaxe. Stand there, and you'll likely see a hulking beast sauntering over with death in their eyes. But the worst of it is when exploring--and more often when fighting--you get caught in a trap meant for beasts, not people. https://www.reddit.com/r/MortalShell/comments/1vwuuro/bear_traps/ As showcased by Redditor Parcori in the above August 24 video, they died after beating the first open-world boss you encounter, the Great Arbiter of Flesh. This is a tough battle, especially because it occurs near the very first beacon in Fainweald, Mortal Shell 2's starting zone. Miss a parry once or twice, and you're likely dead. That's frustrating enough, but what makes it particularly aggravating are the bear traps littered around the arena. These bear traps are literally everywhere! Sometimes in front of enemy camps. Sometimes in front of chests. Sometimes in front of NPCs. Sometimes they're just out in the world, lying in wait like a panther preparing to pounce on its prey. I hate them a lot, and I'm not the only one. "The damn bear traps," Redditor mountainyoo posted on August 20 with a Robot Chicken video of a gummy bear screaming after stepping on a bear trap. "Who else steps on absolutely every bear trap?" PurplePassenger7078 asked in an August 19 Reddit post. "I'm just so used to sprinting in games, and this game punishes me every single time lmao. I think it's a bit excessive in certain areas." "I just started Mortal Shell and all I can say is: BEAR TRAPS," said Redditor Easy_Direction_6076 on August 22, sharing a video of Sideshow Bob from The Simpsons repeatedly stepping on a rake. "Me whenever I spot a bear trap," posted Pointblankadvance on August 20, using a similar video as Easy_Direction_6076. I can't tell you the number of times I've stepped on bear traps while exploring. And it always happens at the worst possible times: low health and mid-fight. Although I'm breezing through the game, there are a handful of bosses that've almost caused me to throw my controller through the TV. Still, what pisses me off more than, say, the Hexapod or Isaac, the Scholar Prince boss fights are ... you guessed it, bear traps. Ugh. Mortal Shell 2 is available now on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. Cold Symmetry recently released a substantial update that nerfed a handful of bosses and made gold more plentiful so you can upgrade your equipment more often.

title: New Indie Fishing Game Is More Popular Than Modern Warfare 4 Beta On Steam
description: Everyone has heard of Call of Duty, and yet, a video game that you've probably never heard of is outperforming the first Modern Warfare 4 beta on Steam. How to Fish looks like a surprise hit with over 341,000 concurrent players today, per Steam. Plus, developer Dazed Games has announced the co-op title has already sold over 1 million copies after launching August 20. It's currently available for just under $5, with a regular $8 price tag. That easily tops the early-access beta for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which hit just over 115,000 concurrent players Friday on Steam and has been declining since then. Keep in mind this first trial with the newest entry in the FPS franchise is for people who preordered Modern Warfare on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. An open beta is set to begin this upcoming weekend, from August 28 to September 1. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YVPYjhBdRbE Meanwhile, How to Fish is a physics-based game about reeling in cod and sharks, then beating them to death by any means necessary. That includes punching the water dwellers, stabbing them, and even no-scope shooting them for more money. So yes, it falls on the silly side compared to a more realistic simulator. Intriguingly, How to Fish has the support of Evil Landfall, the publishing and support side of Peak developer Landfall. That co-op climbing game was one of last year's biggest surprise hits on Steam. Both titles fall under the newish genre called friendslop. Back to Call of Duty, Modern Warfare 4 is set to officially come out October 23. Playing the beta--which includes a campaign mission for the first time ever--can net you some special rewards for the full release. The FPS will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X, and Switch 2.

title: Witcher 4 Release Window Narrowed Down, As Dev Teases “A Surprise Or Two” At Gamescom About Other Things
description: CD Projekt Red has narrowed down the release timing for The Witcher 4, confirming the RPG is coming sometime in 2028. The company revealed this in a new video that sets the table for Gamescom this week. There won't be any Witcher 4 news at Gamescom, but CD Projekt Red will highlight The Witcher 3's new Songs of the Past DLC at the showcase, while there will be "a surprise or two to share" during livestreams planned throughout Gamescom. More than 500 people are working on The Witcher 4 now, CD Projekt Red joint-CEO Michal Nowakowski said in a newly released video. "This is our biggest, boldest, and most ambitious game to date," he said. As for the 2028 release date for The Witcher 4, Nowakowski said, "I know it's a bit of a wait, and you'd love to play it sooner--but let the team cook. It will be worth the wait." https://twitter.com/thewitcher/status/2091908890388541442 The Witcher 4 kicks off a new trilogy of The Witcher games, which will also include The Witcher 5 and The Witcher 6. These will all be released within a six-year window, so the whole new trilogy could be out by 2034. Importantly, Nowakowski said CD Projekt Red is "targeting" a 2028 release for The Witcher 4, so it could be delayed like The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 were before it. In addition to the Songs of the Past expansion for The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red's teams are working on many other games. These include Cyberpunk 2, a new The Witcher game said to be focused on multiplayer, and a game made in partnership with Scopely.

title: GTA 6 Leak Shows Off Apparent Nudist Colony
description: A new clip showing leaked Grand Theft Auto 6 footage has made its way online, and it looks like you're going to be able to visit a nudist colony in Leonida. The clip, which just runs for a few minutes, shows co-protagonist Jason walking near a pool and several hot tubs, with dozens of naked people hanging around and dancing. Some of them seem relatively neutral to Jason's presence, while others are annoyed with the completely clothed man walking around and looking at them with binoculars. That seems like a reasonable reaction. One woman in particular notices Jason leering with binoculars and physically attacks him. Again, reasonable. While we've seen a whole bunch of GTA 6 clips from a still-at-large leaker over the last week, they may not have a particularly negative effect on Rockstar. According to a former technical director at the studio, the vast majority of players don't care about the leaked footage, and it pales in comparison to the controversial Hot Coffee incident that affected Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. Still, Take-Two is actively subpoenaing information related to the leaks in an effort to uncover the leaker's identity. We'll get our first official look at gameplay on August 27, exclusively on Netflix. Grand Theft Auto 6 launches for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

title: GTA 6 Leaks Don’t Matter, So Please Calm Down, Ex-Rockstar Director Says
description: Former Rockstar North director Obbe Vermeij has commented on the many GTA 6 leaks that have emerged over the past week. Vermeij, who was the technical director for GTA 3, GTA: San Andreas, GTA 4, and other titles in the series, told everyone to "clam down" because "the leaks are a nothing burger." He said Rockstar is intentionally staying quiet as part of the company's marketing strategy to generate as much hype as possible for GTA 6, and the leaks are not prompting Rockstar to amend its plans. That's no surprise, as a recent report specifically said Rockstar was not going to alter its marketing plans for GTA 6 due to the spate of leaks coming to light. The Netflix premiere of the game's "extended look" remains scheduled for August 27. Vermeij said the leaks are no big deal in part because "90% of future players don't spend their time on the internet looking for video snippets." He added, "They don't have the time and don't want spoilers." He went on to say the development teams working on GTA 6 are probably "a little annoyed about [the leaks] but not more than that." https://twitter.com/ObbeVermeij/status/2091184776166113568 Vermeij pointed out that he was working at Rockstar the time of the infamous "Hot Coffee" situation surrounding GTA: San Andreas. He said this was a "nightmare" for Rockstar's management team in New York, but didn't affect the developers themselves in Edinburgh at Rockstar North. "The current leaks are far less consequential than Hot Coffee was," he said. "It looks like GTA 6 will be phenomenal and sell for the next 15 years or so. The leaks are just a tiny blip." One of gaming's biggest controversies ever, the Hot Coffee situation saw Rockstar owner Take-Two paying out money to settle suits related to a mod in GTA: San Andreas' PC edition that unlocked an interactive sex minigame. Hillary Clinton, then a Senator from New York, called on the Federal Trade Commission to launch an inquiring into the Hot Coffee mod. Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser said the scandal was "draining and upsetting" for the company. The latest batch of GTA 6 leaks began earlier this month, with gameplay footage claiming to be from the open-world game showing off all manner of characters, activities, and possible new features. One of the latest leaks shows main character Jason visiting what appears to be a nudist colony. Another leak showed that players may need to manually refill their cars with gas. Still other leaks suggested that GTA 6 may have a form of currency that can be traded IRL. Rockstar and Take-Two have yet to identify the person or people responsible for the leak. Whoever they may be, they appear to have access to the game. In 2022, GTA 6 suffered its first major leak of gameplay footage. The autistic 18-year-old suspect was apprehended and ordered to live in a secure hospital for life. In July this year, it was reported that the person, Arion Kurtaj, left the secure hospital and is now in a "normal prison" awaiting a new trial.

title: Final Fantasy Resonance Has More Going For It Than Just Its Impressive Cast
description: Ahead of its release in October, Square Enix has dropped several new details about Final Fantasy Resonance, its HD-2D reimagining of the mobile game Final Fantasy: Brave Exvius. Based on the first season of Brave Exvius, here's a closer look at the game's world, characters, gameplay, vision systems, and completionist content. Empires strike back The Zoldaad Empire has a few defectors.Two of the regions that players can explore include the powerful military nation of Zoldaad and the city of mages known as Mysidia. Just like in Brave Exvius, Zoldaad appears to be on the march as the home of the fabled Fire Crystal, and has secretly been building up a fleet of airships and mass-producing magitek as it expands its borders into neighboring countries. Considered to be a legend, the advanced magical civilization of Mysidia is home to some of the strongest magic-wielders in the world and is said to also house the Ice Crystal. Characters Previous trailers have already shown us the main cast of Final Fantasy Resonance--Rain, Laswell, Fina, Jake, and Lid--and if you played the mobile game, you can also expect to see a few more familiar faces like the Mysidian sage Sakura. Opposing the heroes are the Sworn Six of Paladia, the Veritas. Each Veritas represents an element, and their roster includes the brutish Veritas of Flame, the honorable Veritas of Earth, and the volatile Veritas of Light. Gameplay Classic Final Fantasy gameplay meets retro-inspired visuals.At its core, Final Fantasy Resonance is an old-school turn-based RPG, full of hard-hitting Limit Break attacks and chances to strategically outmaneuver enemies. One of the big draws in the game are the Visions of legendary Final Fantasy heroes, who can fight alongside Rain and his companions when they're summoned. Players may use the magic and abilities of Visions in combat, and the stronger your bond with them grows, the more abilities you'll unlock for these legends. Staggering all enemies in one turn will even allow you to trigger a Resonance with a vision, resulting in them performing an exceptionally devastating attack--while your eyes get treated to a slick piece of CG animation. You can even make your Visions stronger, but there's a catch: You'll need magicite to grant them stronger abilities, but because the material is exceedingly rare, you'll have to choose which Vision you strengthen. Some of the Visions also include original characters that were first introduced in Brave Exvius: Amelia: A maid armed with Fire-aspected guns Camille: A mercenary who uses water and earth attacks Wilhelm: An imperial general who can act as a party's shield Victoria: A black mage who wields dark magic Ayaka: A white mage who can buff the party with support and healing magic As mentioned above, heroes from previous Final Fantasy games can also be recruited to your party: Firion (Final Fantasy) Onion Knight (Final Fantasy 3) Vaan (Final Fantasy 12) Lightning (Final Fantasy 13) Noctis (Final Fantasy 15) Clive Rosfield (Final Fantasy 16) Espers Don't mess with Espers.For some extra firepower, you can also summon Espers. These powerful beings will join your battle for three turns, and once the timer is up, they'll drop a devastating attack before they vanish. The cuddly Carbuncle will cast Reflect magic on your party, the sea serpent Leviathan will deal water damage to enemies with a Tsunami, the armor-clad Odin can dish out a non-elemental attack that might instakill some enemies, and the mighty dragon Bahamut unleashes his signature Megaflare assault on foes. Completionist content Ultima Weapon is going to kick butt...mostly yours.Anyone looking to 100% Final Fantasy Resonance will want to make certain their party is ready to fight. Square Enix is teasing a battle with the mysterious bladesman Gilgamesh, and if you're feeling really confident, you can even challenge Ultima Weapon. A boss battle that has cropped up in several Final Fantasy games over the decades, Ultima Weapon demands perfect preparation, or you can expect your challenge to be over in just a few short turns. Final Fantasy Resonance launches for PC and consoles on October 22.

title: The Blood Of Dawnwalker Devs Heard Your 60fps Requests And Have Good News For Console Players
description: If you wanted to play The Blood of Dawnwalker at 60fps, you'd originally need to get the PC version and hope your rig was up to scratch. Developer Rebel Wolves didn't initially list a 60fps mode for Xbox Series X, PS5, and PS5 Pro when it recently released a quick look at the graphical modes for those consoles, but the developer says it will now be added via a day-one patch when the game launches in September. "Performance mode was already in the works, but it was still being tested. We simply weren’t ready to promise it yet," Rebel Wolves wrote on its The Blood of Dawnwalker X account. "We heard your feedback. It was clear how much this mattered to many of you, so we focused on finishing the next round of tests. Those results gave us the confidence we needed to confirm Performance Mode for Day one." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yLMUp83HZKE The Blood of Dawnwalker will have three modes to choose from on Xbox Series X, PS5, and PS5 Pro: Performance targets 60fps, Balanced targets 40fps, and Quality targets 30fps. Xbox Series S owners are only getting one mode, which targets 30fps on the lower-spec hardware. Rebel Wolves hasn't detailed the major differences between the modes either, but typically, Performance mode prioritizes a higher, smoother frame rate while cutting back on fancier lighting effects, simpler particle effects, and less detail compared to Quality mode. Balanced mode attempts to have the best of both worlds while targeting 40fps, while the PS5 Pro has proven to be a 4K 60fps powerhouse after the rollout of an upgraded PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution earlier this year. Out on September 3, The Blood of Dawnwalker is the debut game from Rebel Wolves, a studio that features several former Witcher and Cyberpunk 2077 developers in its roster, including The Witcher 3 game director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz. Set in a dark medieval world full of vampires and grim fantasy, players will have to grapple with the consequences of their actions as they build up power for a final showdown against the vampire lord Brencis. "Whether you're talking to your best friend, working to bandage an injured comrade, or battling opponents to save your father's life, when the hunger takes hold, your actions may suddenly be out of your control. Dawnwalker is a game all about making you live with the consequences," Phil Hornshaw wrote in GameSpot's The Blood of Dawnwalker preview.

Call Of Duty’s Most Controversial Item Is Back In Modern Warfare 4, But With Some Major Changes
description: One of the most infamous and controversial items in Call of Duty is the Riot Shield. Some love it. Some hate it. Well, it's back in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, but with a few key changes. With MW4's beta now live, we're seeing the game in action and learning more about it. This includes new details on the Riot Shield, including how it's now destructible. Not only that, but the new Riot Shield can be placed on the ground to allow players to create their own cover, wherever they are. What's more, the Riot Shield is now unlocked as a field upgrade as opposed to occupying a weapon slot. https://twitter.com/InfinityWard/status/2090852829409763502 "In use, the shield provides frontal protection while advancing or holding a position. It can also be used offensively, with a new heavy melee attack that knocks enemies down and creates space in close quarters," Activision said. When planted in the ground, players can mount their weapons to it for improved stability. The Riot Shield can also be used strategically in MW4's objective-based modes where players hunker down in one particular spot. To balance things out, Activision made the Riot Shield destructible in MW4. In the past, it could soak up bullets like a sponge, and people loved and hated that. In MW4, it's "durable enough to support a push or cover a retreat." However, it will eventually break, and Activision said that should encourage players to use it strategically as opposed to opting for "sustained use." The MW4 beta is going on now for people who preordered the game. An open beta, meanwhile, runs August 28-September 1, and that doesn't require any preorder. The beta includes not just multiplayer, but also a campaign mission, Entrenched, and a glimpse at the future of Call of Duty: Warzone. MW4 launches in full on October 23 for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC, and Switch 2. It's the first game since 2013's Call of Duty: Ghosts to be released on a Nintendo platform.

title: GTA 6 Leaker Has Not Been Identified Yet – Report
description: One of the biggest stories in gaming this week has been the ongoing GTA 6 gameplay leaks, which are all about hyping up a memecoin for profit. A new report provides insight into how Rockstar is handling the situation internally. Bloomberg reported that Rockstar has yet to identify the party responsible, or how such a breach happened. One top executive at Rockstar sent a memo to staff this week "denouncing the leaker and promising the incident wouldn't detract from the excellent work they've done," the report said. Additionally, it was reported that Rockstar is not planning to change its marketing plans for GTA 6 due to the leak. Some had theorized that the leak might have some effect on the planned reveal on Netflix on August 27, but that's apparently not going to be the case. After GTA 6's first trailer leaked in December 2023, Rockstar responded in real time and released the trailer ahead of schedule, so there is precedent to Rockstar altering plans based on leaks. GTA 6 suffered a massive leak in 2022. At the time, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said it was “really frustrating and upsetting,” but the leaks had no financial impact on the company. Take-Two lost more than $2 billion in its total value this week since the latest leaks began, but there could be any number of different reasons for that apart from the leaks. It has also come to light that Take-Two, which owns Rockstar and the GTA franchise, subpoenaed Microsoft and Discord as part of its effort to hunt down the party or parties responsible for the leak. GTA 6 is set for release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
